description.en: Combines two files into one tidy table and documents every change.
description.es: Combina dos archivos en una sola tabla ordenada y documenta cada cambio.

label.en: How should the rows be matched? (e.g. same customer ID, or just stack them)
label.es: ¿Cómo se deben emparejar las filas? (p. ej. mismo ID de cliente, o solo apilarlas)

nodes.text:
Combine two files into one tidy table. First file: {{fileA}}. Second file: {{fileB}} (both inside data/). How to match rows: {{matchBy}}

Do this:
1. Inspect both files (sheets, headers, types, duplicates, blanks, different spellings of the same thing). Never change the originals.
2. Clean copies: trim spaces, standardise names, dates, numbers and codes, align column names that mean the same thing, and remove exact duplicates.
3. Merge as the user described. Keep unmatched rows (do not silently drop data) and add a column 'source' or 'match_status' showing where each row came from or whether it matched. Report how many rows matched, only-in-A and only-in-B.
4. Write outputs/merged.xlsx with a 'Merged' sheet (formatted, filters, frozen header) and a 'Changes' sheet with the counts of each fix.
5. Write outputs/changes.md: a change log in plain language (what was cleaned, what was merged, how conflicts were resolved, rows needing human review) plus your assumptions.

GROUND RULES (follow strictly):
- Any user-provided input file lives in data/ inside this project. NEVER modify, move or delete the originals: work on copies inside the project.
- Put every deliverable in outputs/ (create the folder if needed). Do not write deliverables anywhere else.
- Prefer Python. Use the Python packages already installed globally; create a virtual environment (python -m venv .venv) ONLY if a needed package is missing, and pip install ONLY what you need from: openpyxl pandas xlsxwriter matplotlib python-docx. If Python is not installed or cannot be run, say so plainly in one short message and STOP (do not try to install Python yourself).
- Do not ask questions mid-way unless you are truly blocked. Instead, make sensible choices and write your assumptions down in the deliverable and in your final message.
- Write the deliverables and the final message in the same language as the user's request (Spanish or English).
- Be safe: do not run anything destructive, do not touch files outside this project, do not send data over the network (except where this task explicitly needs web search).
- FINISH with a short plain-language summary for a non-technical person: what you produced, where it is (exact paths under outputs/), the assumptions you made, and anything they should double-check.

nodes.message: Open outputs/merged.xlsx and read outputs/changes.md. Approve if the merge is right.
